title: Judged on love
hook: John's saying: in the evening of life, we will be examined on love
tomorrow: how many ways can one poem say what prayer is?

segments.voice: Yesterday, where have you hidden?: a lover already reached, going out calling. Same John today, and the last exam of all.

Study guide, practice test, the night-before cram. Most exams at least tell you the subject. John of the Cross wrote one short line about the last exam of all, and he gave the subject away. In his Spanish: "A la tarde te examinarán en el amor." In the evening, you will be examined on love. One subject. And here's the odd part. In the Gospel scene behind that line, the people who pass have no idea they were ever taking the test.
screen: `THE NIGHT-BEFORE CRAM.` → `IN THE EVENING: LOVE.` → `THEY DIDN'T KNOW IT WAS A TEST.`

segments.voice: The scene is Matthew 25. A king separates people, the way a shepherd separates sheep from goats, and tells one group why they're welcome: "I was an hungred, and ye gave me meat: I was thirsty, and ye gave me drink: I was a stranger, and ye took me in." Sick, and you visited. In prison, and you came. And they're baffled. "Lord, when saw we thee an hungred, and fed thee?" They don't remember doing any of it for him. Then the answer: "Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me." Now the strange detail gets stranger. The other group asks the very same question: when? Nobody on either side knew. So the puzzle solves itself. The exam isn't on what you can recite under pressure. It's on what you did for whoever was in front of you, mostly without noticing. John's saying goes on, in a paraphrase: learn to love the way God wants to be loved. That turns the verdict into a study plan. Christians read Matthew 25 as a picture of the last judgment, and also as a map for this afternoon.
screen: `HUNGRY, THIRSTY, A STRANGER.` · `LORD, WHEN SAW WE THEE?` · `BOTH SIDES ASK WHEN.` · `A VERDICT BECOMES A STUDY PLAN.` · then, large: `EXAMINED ON LOVE.`

segments.voice: Run back through today from the moment you woke. On your fingers, count the small moments someone needed something: a reply, a ride, a little patience. Don't grade them; just notice which ones you met and which slipped past. If you pray, you can hand the whole day over, the slipped ones too.
Judged on love. John's evening exam: one subject, and the ones who pass never knew they were sitting it.
Hold on to this: examined on love, a test you don't cram for because you're already sitting it. That's today.

howItsDone: Many Christians end the day with an examination of conscience, looking back over the hours; Matthew 25's list of feeding, welcoming and visiting is also the root of what Catholics call the corporal works of mercy.

myth: 'in the evening we will be examined on love' is a Bible verse
it's one of John of the Cross's short sayings. the Gospel scene behind it is Matthew 25.
in Matthew 25, the people welcomed by the king don't remember serving him
they ask, baffled: Lord, when saw we thee an hungred, and fed thee?
only the people sent away ask 'when?'
both groups ask the same question. nobody on either side knew.

fork.setup: your cousin says, 'judgment day is basically a pop quiz on Bible facts.' you open Matthew 25. what does the king actually ask about?
options: the hungry fed, the stranger taken in, the sick visited.
which verses each person could recite from memory.
how often each person went to church services.
fork.reveal: the king names meat, drink, a stranger taken in, the sick and the prisoner visited, and the people who did it didn't know it counted.

original.note: Greek: the least. the king's word in Matthew 25:40 for the ones he calls his brethren.

trapdoor: what you thought: judgment day is a test of right answers.
what it means: John names one subject, love; and in Matthew 25 the ones who pass didn't know they were taking it.
what a scholar hears: 'a la tarde' is the evening, the close of a workday; John's sayings are numbered differently in different editions.
guess: John's saying: life's last exam has one subject, love
a church court where monks were tried on their charity
a rule that confession must list sins against love first

chat.says: Pop's out of surgery. i skipped AP review to sit with him and now i'll bomb bio. dumb?
options: Not dumb. Study tonight, but John says the evening exam is on love, and you showed up.
Kind of. Love means being responsible, so the review should have come first.
Doesn't matter. God only grades effort, so the bio test won't count anyway.
chat.meaning: John: in the evening we're examined on love. Sitting with Pop counted. It doesn't cancel studying tonight.

John of the Cross.meaning: a Spanish Carmelite friar and poet

inasmuch.meaning: old English: to the extent that, insofar as

brethren.meaning: an old plural of brother: family, kin
